Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0060", "row_sha256": "8e119eacf5fd9d0f22906af672edcc080c41fe90e3309ae05fadf01369d02c59", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you turn these notes into one clear ordinary update for the Northbank Volunteer Transport group, for the week ending sunday 19 october 2025, with the rota dates being monday 20 october through sunday 2 november. it should sound like an update someone in the group would actually send, not a report written from outside. i'm trying to get the booking picture and the next couple of weeks in one place, because the information is in the paper rota, jo's messages and the new spreadsheet, and people are mixing up what happened last week with what is still to be covered. keep the distinction between a trip that was cancelled by a rider, one moved to a later date, and one that nobody has been able to match. those are not interchangeable. don't turn the remaining unmatched trips into cancelled trips just because they are still open.

for the driver picture, there are 18 active volunteer drivers. twelve have confirmed that they can take at least some shifts during the coming two weeks, four have told jo vale they are unavailable for that whole period, and two have not replied yet. don't describe all twelve as available every day, because their individual days and times differ. one of the people who hasn't replied might normally help on tuesday mornings, but we don't have a confirmation from them, so don't count that as coverage. jo is the rota coordinator and is fitting the trips around the times people actually offered. she isn't a full-time dispatcher; she also has her usual volunteer shifts. say that plainly if it helps explain why the rota is being updated in batches rather than instantly.

last week there were 31 ride requests. twenty-four trips were completed: 10 were for health appointments, 7 for grocery shopping, 4 for pharmacy visits and 3 for social visits. three riders cancelled their own trips before they took place. two requests were moved to the following week at the riders' request, and two requests had no driver matched by sunday evening. please keep those figures together in a numbered section if that reads naturally, and make clear that the 24 completed trips are a different count from the 31 requests. one open request is a tuesday morning pickup for Eastbank Clinic; the other is a friday afternoon trip from Alder Court for groceries. they are still requests, not promises that a driver will be found.

we logged 612 miles on the completed trips last week. jo has received 19 mileage forms so far and is still waiting for five; the missing forms don't change the trip count, and don't imply that the remaining forms have been approved or paid. the cars used are drivers' own cars. the group does not have a wheelchair-accessible vehicle, which matters when new requests are discussed, but don't suggest any particular ride was refused for that reason because that isn't in these notes. we use a printed rota in the dispatch room as well as phone messages. on 14 october jo started a shared spreadsheet trial for driver availability, mostly so she can see offers and changes in one place. it is an aid for arranging the rota, not a replacement for checking with a driver.

there are two newer volunteers, Priya Das and Martin Cole. they completed the group orientation on 16 october, but each still needs one accompanied practice journey before taking a booking alone. don't call them fully cleared to drive passengers solo. jo is trying to arrange the practice journeys around their work schedules, but no dates have been set. Helen Ward has given a useful example of why a single label like available isn't enough; her exact message was, “I can do Thursday afternoons, but not before lunch.” put that in as a normal short quote if it fits, and don't change the wording or make it sound like she offered all-day Thursday.

there have also been a couple of practical details from the week that belong in the update. a rider asked whether the driver can wait during a clinic appointment, and jo said that depends on the length of the appointment and the driver's next booking, so the person arranging the trip should ask when they call rather than assume waiting is included. on 17 october a grocery trip took longer than expected because the rider needed help carrying bags from the car to the entrance; the driver was able to help that time. don't make this a general promise that every driver can carry bags or assist inside a building. another driver reported that the printed rota showed an earlier pickup time than jo's later phone message for one trip; jo checked directly with the rider and corrected the paper copy. there wasn't a missed trip, so don't imply that there was.

please make the update easy to scan without making it stiff. use short connected paragraphs, and headings where they help. the numbered booking section should show requests, completed trips with the four service categories, rider cancellations, moved requests, and unmatched requests. explain that the two unmatched bookings remain open. include the driver count and the difference between confirmed, unavailable and not-yet-replied drivers, and mention the practical status of Priya and Martin. keep the mileage forms separate from trip outcomes. the spreadsheet, paper rota and phone-check process can sit together as a brief coordination note. don't add details about passengers, destinations, costs, medical conditions, or reasons for the unavailable drivers beyond what i've given.

for the ending, include a provisional assessment of the next two weeks, not a verdict about the whole service: based on the current information, ordinary daytime coverage looks workable only if the two drivers who have not replied confirm some shifts and the usual eastside tuesday-morning volunteer is back in the rota. that is a conditional assessment, not confirmation that either thing has happened. its scope is routine daytime trips during 20 october to 2 november; it does not assess evenings, weekends as a general category, emergency journeys, or the group's longer-term ability to serve riders. keep that whole limitation with the assessment, and leave it as the final paragraph rather than adding a separate upbeat wrap-up or a broader conclusion.", "output": "Write one clear, ordinary update for the Northbank Volunteer Transport group, covering the week ending Sunday 19 October 2025 and the rota period Monday 20 October through Sunday 2 November. Use the voice of a group member sharing a practical update. Make the information easy to scan with short connected paragraphs and helpful headings, while keeping the tone natural rather than formal. Distinguish last week’s completed trips and booking outcomes from the trips still to be covered.

### Booking picture

There were 31 ride requests last week. Twenty-four trips were completed: 10 for health appointments, 7 for grocery shopping, 4 for pharmacy visits and 3 for social visits. Three riders cancelled their own trips before they took place. Two requests were moved to the following week at the riders’ request. Two requests remained unmatched by Sunday evening. Make clear that the 24 completed trips are a count of completed trips, not the total number of requests, and that cancellations, moved requests and unmatched requests are separate outcomes.

The two unmatched requests remain open, not cancelled: one is a Tuesday morning pickup for Eastbank Clinic, and the other is a Friday afternoon grocery trip from Alder Court. Do not imply that a driver has been found for either one.

### Rota and coordination

There are 18 active volunteer drivers. For the coming two weeks, 12 have confirmed that they can take some shifts, 4 have told rota coordinator Jo Vale that they are unavailable for the whole period, and 2 have not replied. The 12 confirmed drivers have different days and times available; do not describe them as available every day. One driver who has not replied might normally help on Tuesday mornings, but that is not confirmed coverage. Jo fits trips around the times drivers have actually offered. She is the rota coordinator, not a full-time dispatcher, and also has her usual volunteer shifts; mention this if useful in explaining that rota updates come in batches rather than instantly.

The group uses a printed rota in the dispatch room and phone messages. On 14 October, Jo began a shared-spreadsheet trial to keep driver availability and changes visible in one place. The spreadsheet helps arrange the rota but does not replace checking with a driver.

### Volunteers and practical details

Priya Das and Martin Cole completed group orientation on 16 October. Each still needs one accompanied practice journey before taking a booking alone. Jo is trying to arrange these around their work schedules, but no dates have been set. Do not describe either volunteer as cleared to drive passengers solo.

Helen Ward’s message illustrates why availability needs to be stated by day and time: “I can do Thursday afternoons, but not before lunch.” Include it as a short, ordinary quote without changing its wording or implying that she offered all-day Thursday.

The group uses drivers’ own cars and does not have a wheelchair-accessible vehicle. This matters when new requests are discussed, but the notes do not say that any particular ride was refused for this reason. A rider asked whether a driver could wait during a clinic appointment. Jo said that depends on the appointment’s length and the driver’s next booking, so the person arranging the trip should ask when they call rather than assume waiting is included.

On 17 October, a grocery trip took longer than expected because the rider needed help carrying bags from the car to the entrance; the driver was able to help on that occasion. Do not turn this into a general promise that all drivers can carry bags or assist inside a building. One driver also reported that the printed rota showed an earlier pickup time than Jo’s later phone message. Jo checked directly with the rider and corrected the paper copy. No trip was missed.

### Mileage

The completed trips logged 612 miles last week. Jo has received 19 mileage forms and is waiting for five more. Keep the forms separate from trip outcomes: the missing forms do not change the number of trips, and the notes do not establish that any remaining forms have been approved or paid.

End with this provisional assessment as the final paragraph: based on the current information, ordinary daytime coverage during 20 October to 2 November looks workable only if the two drivers who have not replied confirm some shifts and the usual eastside Tuesday-morning volunteer is back in the rota. Make clear that this is conditional, and that neither condition is confirmed to have happened. Limit the assessment to routine daytime trips during those dates; it does not assess evenings, weekends as a general category, emergency journeys, or the group’s longer-term ability to serve riders. Do not add a separate upbeat wrap-up or a broader conclusion."}]
